identity.title: SoftJAX & SoftTorch: Empowering Automatic Differentiation Libraries with Informative Gradients

problem.claim: Hard primitives in automatic-differentiation libraries can produce zero or undefined gradients that are unhelpful for optimization.

gap.claim: Existing soft relaxations are fragmented across projects, making them difficult to combine and compare.

contributions.claim: Introduces SoftJAX and SoftTorch, open-source libraries for soft differentiable programming, with soft functions serving as drop-in replacements for hard JAX and PyTorch operations.
Provides soft elementwise, Boolean/index, and axiswise operators, using fuzzy logic, optimal transport, or permutahedron projections, and supports straight-through gradient estimation.
Makes a toolbox of soft relaxations accessible within differentiable programming.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish the work as introducing open-source, feature-complete SoftJAX and SoftTorch libraries that consolidate soft differentiable-programming functionality.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report benchmarking and a practical case study as demonstrations of the libraries.

narrative_sequence.summary: AD frameworks enable gradient-based optimization across scientific fields.
Hard primitives may yield zero or undefined gradients, while soft-relaxation implementations remain fragmented.
The work introduces SoftJAX and SoftTorch with broad soft-operation coverage and straight-through estimation support.
The authors report benchmarking and a practical case study demonstrating access to the consolidated toolbox.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a concrete optimization obstacle to a fragmented implementation landscape, then describes a unified library organized by operator families and gradient-estimation support.

lessons.interpretation: This structure helps align a systems contribution with both the user-facing problem and the capabilities needed to address it.
lessons.application: For a similar library paper, map each stated limitation to an explicit capability category and identify the demonstration used for each category.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the work centers on one algorithm or theoretical result rather than an integrated toolkit.

unknowns: No quantitative benchmark results, baselines, datasets, or case-study details are given.
The abstract does not specify what makes the libraries feature-complete or how their implementations compare in practice.
